BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO (BARMM)
Old (For Years 2023 and below) Source: PIDSR Manual of Procedure 2014

Suspect
A person with acute diarrhea with visible blood in the stool

Suspect
Disease unknown in the area: A person aged 5 years or more with severe dehydration or who died from acute watery diarrhea, OR
Disease endemic in the area: A person aged 5 years or more with acute watery diarrhea with or without vomiting, OR
In an area where there is a cholera epidemic: A person with acute watery diarrhea, with or without vomiting.

Confirmed
A suspected case that is laboratory-confirmed, through isolation of Vibrio cholerae 01 or 0139 from stools in any patient with diarrhea.

Suspect
A person with an illness characterized by insidious onset of sustained fever, headache, malaise, anorexia, relative bradycardia, constipation or diarrhea, and non-productive cough for 5 days or more.

Probable
A suspected case that is positive in Typhoid Rapid Diagnostic Test; OR
A suspected case that is epidemiologically linked to a confirmed case in an outbreak.

Confirmed
A suspected or probable case that is laboratory confirmed.
Laboratory confirmation by culture or molecular methods of Salmonella Typhi or detection of Salmonella Typhi or Salmonella Paratyphi DNA from a normally sterile site.

Suspect
A person with acute illness characterized by acute jaundice, dark urine, loss of appetite, body weakness, extreme fatigue, and right upper quadrant tenderness.

Confirmed
A suspected case that is laboratory-confirmed.

Laboratory Confirmation:
Hepatitis A: Positive for IgM anti-HAV
Hepatitis B: Positive for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) or positive for IgM anti-HBc and antiHBe
Non-A, non-B: Negative for IgM anti-HAV and IgM anti-HBs (or HBsAg)
Hepatitis C: Positive for anti-HCV
Hepatitis D: HBsAg positive or IgM anti-HBc positive PLUS anti-HDV positive (only as co-infection or super-infection of hepa B)
Hepatitis E: IgM anti-HEV positive"

Suspect:
A person with acute diarrhea with visible blood in the stool

Confirmed Case:
A suspect case with stool positive for bacterial or parasitic pathogens (i.e., Shigella dysenteriae type 1, Entamoeba histolytica or Escherichia coli) through bacterial culture or any molecular diagnostic test.

Suspect:
In area/s where cholera outbreak has not been declared: Any patient aged 2 years and above presenting with acute watery diarrhea and severe dehydration or dying from acute watery diarrhea
In area/s where cholera outbreak is declared: Any person presenting with or dying from acute watery diarrhea. (WHO GTFCC: Interim Guidance Document on Cholera Surveillance 2017)

Probable Case:
A suspected cholera case with positive cholera RDT result.

Confirmed:
A suspect case that is laboratory-confirmed, thru isolation of Vibrio cholerae O1 or O139 from stools in any patient with diarrhea (EB PIDSR MOP 2014)
